title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, November 2026 — the last MBOS inside the December FOMC's information set, and the pre-cliff control month, 8:30 a.m. ET
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events?release=manufacturing-business-outlook-survey — the Philadelphia Fed's own filtered release calendar, fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200, 130,695 bytes) by this event's own never-assessed initial research. Its embedded structured data carries the row verbatim as `{"title":"November Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey","month":"november 2026","day":"19","displayMonth":"Nov","year":"2026","time":"8:30 a.m."}` — so the date and the time are READ from the primary, not derived. The same payload enumerates all twelve 2026 MBOS rows (Jan 15 · Feb 19 · Mar 19 · Apr 16 · May 21 · Jun 18 · Jul 16 · Aug 20 · Sep 17 · Oct 15 · Nov 19 · Dec 17), every one at 8:30 a.m. and every one the third Thursday of its month, which matches the bank's own published cadence rule read the same day at philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/mbos-faqs (HTTP 200, 55,921 bytes): "We usually publish the results at 8:30 a.m. ET on the third Thursday of each month, barring holidays." November 2026's Thursdays are 5/12/19/26, so the 19th is the third; rule and enumeration agree on 12 of 12 monthly observations. Filed estimate on the same two counts every sibling regional-survey entry records, NEITHER of which is doubt about the date: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-10
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-10 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/philly-fed-mfg-2026-11-19.from-survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16.json, filed 2026-09-09 by the SPF lane) and discharged BOTH tasks that proposal assigned to whoever wrote this file. (a) The date and the 8:30 a.m. time are read from the primary — the MBOS-specific landing page could NOT supply them (its Release Calendar panel publishes only the next release, on 2026-09-10 still `Sep 17 2026`), so the filtered calendar endpoint is the enumerating surface, and the proposal's incidental finding is reproduced: the `?release=` query string is client-side and the filtered URL returns the whole-calendar body. (b) The tier question is ANSWERED AND THE PREMISE IS FALSE. The proposal asked whether landing inside the pre-blackout window changes the tier; the Philadelphia Fed publishes its blackout dates verbatim on that same calendar payload — 2026 including "November 28-December 10" — so 2026-11-19 sits NINE DAYS CLEAR of blackout and is not inside it. Impact stays LOW and symbols [] matched to philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17.json, -2026-10-15.json and -2026-12-17.json, on grounds this ledger measures rather than inherits: the survey is a sub-state qualitative diffusion index of the Third District whose headline explains R-squared of about 0.20 of national manufacturing IP growth since 2015 (measured by the 10-15 sibling), no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is macro-keyed, and none of the nine tracked names carries a Third District manufacturing channel. What earns the row is TIMING, which is an information property and not an impact one. Of the four MBOS prints after 2026-09-10, this is the LAST one inside the 2026-12-09 FOMC's information set (December's lands 12-17, eight days after the meeting) and the last before the 11-25 pre-FOMC Beige Book; its collection window, from the bank's twice-published rule "an eight-day period that closes the Monday prior to publication", is Mon 2026-11-09 to Mon 2026-11-16 — entirely AFTER the 2026-11-03 midterms (a 6-day gap) and entirely BEFORE the 2026-12-12 funding lapse, which makes it December's fully-funded pre-cliff control month; and it is the manufacturing input to the Q4 2026 Price and Inflation Expectations Survey of 2026-11-25, whose day-after-the-quarter's-NBOS construction rule this session reproduced 4 for 4 from the same enumerated payload. Three plausible stories about that timing were MEASURED AND KILLED on the bank's own 700-month bos_history.csv: a midterm November is not noisier (mean absolute Oct-to-Nov headline change 8.81 vs 8.19 for all non-November months, Welch t = 0.34, n=14), November carries no seasonal tilt (8.01 vs 8.19, t = -0.22), and a federal holiday inside the collection window — Veterans Day 2026-11-11 is mid-window, the only 2026 window with one strictly inside — leaves no mark either (7.94 vs 8.36, t = -0.68, n=201). This is an ESTIMATE: it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
